p-36.title: The assumptions on local gauge data
p-36.anchor: We define *local gauge data* to be exactly this information
p-36.body:
At $t=0$, the functions $t$ and $2t$ have the same value. One differentiation gives $1$ and $2$. A jet records the value and every derivative at a point, so a transformation law can use the slope as well as the value.

Do the field-strength calculation under The abelian theory first. Then compare the constant identity with $U(t)=\operatorname{diag}(e^{it},e^{-it})$. Both equal the identity at zero, so their conjugation terms agree there. The varying choice adds $iU'(0)=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1)$ to the time component of the potential.

Starting from zero potential leaves just this derivative term. In `LocalGaugeData`, `maurerCartan_structure` requires that this pure-gauge term have zero curvature, and `maurerCartan_cocycle` requires that successive transformations by $V$ and $U$ agree with the transformation by $UV$. Lean takes the jet types and these laws as inputs. Construction from a Lie group is marked TODO.

p-53.title: Evaluating constant jets
p-53.body:
Turn $7$ into the constant function $t\mapsto 7$, then evaluate at zero to get $7$ back. Every number can be recovered this way. Two constant functions that agree at zero came from the same number.

In `LocalGaugeData`, the same round trip is `eval_ofConstant`. The first observation gives `eval_surjective` and the second gives `ofConstant_injective`. `evalLie_ofConstantLie` does the same for Lie algebra values. To prove `adjoint_bracket`, Lean applies the jet-level identity to constant jets and evaluates. In `deriv_adjointJ_ofConstant`, the derivative rule simplifies because the Maurer–Cartan term of a constant transformation is zero.

p-58.title: Repeated directions in an iterated derivative
p-58.anchor: the iterated derivative ∂_s applies ∂_μ once for each μ in s
p-58.body:
Differentiate $t(2+3t)$ twice at zero and get $6$. The product rule gives two copies of $3$, one for each choice of which derivative hits the factor $t$. The term that still carries that factor vanishes at zero.

`evalLie_iteratedDeriv_mulCoord` counts those choices with `s.count μ` for the centred coordinate $x_\mu$. Each choice leaves the directions `s.erase μ` to act on the other factor. `iteratedDeriv` uses a multiset of directions because the derivatives commute. In `iteratedDeriv_bracket`, Lean uses `s.antidiagonal` to count the ways derivatives can land on the two inputs, including repeated splits.

p-64.title: How morphisms preserve the adjoint action
p-64.anchor: It intertwines Ad on 𝔤 and 𝔤'
p-64.body:
Conjugate a two-by-two matrix by the diagonal matrix with entries $1$ and $-1$. Its off-diagonal entries change sign. Swap the basis vectors of both matrices first and you get the same result in the new basis. Conjugation and the change of basis can be done in either order.

`LocalGaugeData.Hom` gives compatible maps on the groups and Lie algebras of values and of jets. In `Hom.lie_adjoint`, Lean lifts both inputs to constant jets, moves the maps past the jet adjoint action, then evaluates. `Hom.lieJ_iteratedDeriv` moves the jet Lie algebra map past one derivative at a time. Physlib marks the construction from a Lie group homomorphism as TODO.

p-71.title: Why an abelian gauge shift preserves field strength
p-71.anchor: Gauge transformations leave the field strength invariant
p-71.body:
Take $\chi(t,y)=ty$ with time $t$ and space $y$. Its raised gradient $(y,-t)$ gives zero field strength. The Minkowski metric flips the spatial sign, so the time–space component $F^{01}=\partial_t A^1+\partial_y A^0$ is $-1+1=0$. Using the bare gradient $(y,t)$ gives $1+1=2$, as Lean computes in `toFieldStrength_eval_bareGradient_inl_inr`.

Check the signs by doing the same calculation with both indices down. The potential then has components $A_0=y$ and $A_1=t$. The lower-index formula subtracts the two mixed partials, so $F_{01}=1-1=0$. Getting $2$ is a sign that the lower components went into the upper-index formula.

`toFieldStrength_ofGradient` proves the cancellation for every twice continuously differentiable $\chi$, using equality of mixed partials. `toFieldStrength_gaugeTransform` then uses additivity of field strength for differentiable $A$ to show that adding this pure-gauge potential leaves the field strength unchanged at every point.

p-82.title: The product group and its central subgroup
p-82.anchor: a central discrete subgroup of sixth roots of unity
p-82.body:
Take the sixth root of unity $-1$. Physlib sends it to $(I_3,-I_2,-1)$, where $I_3$ and $I_2$ are identity matrices. This triple commutes with every element of the product. Both matrices are scalar multiples of the identities, and complex numbers in the last factor commute.

On a left-handed lepton doublet the weak factor gives $-1$ and integer-normalized hypercharge $-3$ gives $(-1)^{-3}=-1$. The two signs cancel. In `GaugeGroupI`, the map sends $\alpha$ to $(\alpha^2 I_3,\alpha^{-3} I_2,\alpha)$. Its range is `gaugeGroupℤ₆SubGroup`, central by `gaugeGroupℤ₆SubGroup_le_center`.
